title: Sparse-range perfect hash join that keeps the bloom filter
hypothesis: In q16 the HASH_JOIN ps_partkey = p_partkey takes 0.15s CPU to probe 1.236M rows into a 296k-row build. That is about 125ns/row and the second-largest operator after HASH_GROUP_BY (0.31s). The build keys are unique integers with filtered min/max about [2, 2M], so the range is about 2M, roughly 7x the count. PerfectHashJoinExecutor::CanDoPerfectHashJoin (perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:108) rejects any range over a fixed MAX_BUILD_SIZE of 1048576, so the join falls back to the generic HT: it hashes, probes chains, compares keys and gathers the VARCHAR, uhugeint and utinyint payload row by row. A perfect HJ probe is one range check plus a bitmap test per row, and it emits the build columns as dictionary vectors over a reusable dictionary (ProbePerfectHashTable :269), with no per-row gather. Today, though, choosing a perfect HJ also turns off the BF: CanUseBloomFilter returns false when is_perfect_hashtable (physical_hash_join.cpp:769), and the BF only gets filled in JoinHashTable::InsertHashes during ScheduleFinalize, which the perfect path skips. If we just raised the cap, the partsupp scan would emit all 8M rows instead of 1.24M. So the change must keep the BF when the perfect table is sparse.
plan: 1) perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp CanDoPerfectHashJoin: keep the 1M cap, and also accept range <= 2^23 when range <= 16 * ht.Count() and range * (sum of rhs_output_columns type widths + 1) <= ~256MB. Record `perfect_join_statistics.is_sparse = range > 2 * ht.Count()` (new field in perfect_hash_join_executor.hpp PerfectHashJoinStats). Also fix the off-by-one in the duplicate check: compare Count() against build_range + 1. 2) physical_hash_join.cpp PhysicalHashJoin::Finalize (~line 1004-1020): when use_perfect_hash && is_sparse, call FinalizeFilters with is_perfect_hashtable=false, so the BF is requested (SetBuildBloomFilter + deferred_bloom_filters). Then fill the BF directly, since ScheduleFinalize is skipped. FullScanHashTable already has `build_vector` (all build keys from ScanKeyColumn). Hash it with VectorOperations::Hash, which is the same hash the HT stores per row and the scan BF probe uses, then call ht.bloom_filter.Initialize(context, ht.Count()) and bloom_filter.InsertHashes in STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE slices. Finally run the same loop as HashJoinFinalizeEvent::FinishEvent (line 587) to PushBloomFilter for each deferred entry. Do this before returning from Finalize. Expose a small helper on PerfectHashJoinExecutor or JoinHashTable for it. 3) Dense perfect HJs (range <= 2*count) keep today's behaviour of no BF. Verify with EXPLAIN ANALYZE on q16: the join should run as a perfect HJ, the partsupp scan should still show `IN BF` and emit about 1.24M rows, and HASH_JOIN CPU should drop. Correctness tests: duplicate build keys (must fall back), NULL build keys, an empty build side, a negative min, and a build side with VARCHAR payload.
expected_gain: q16: HASH_JOIN 0.15s down to about 0.03-0.05s CPU, so wall about -6..-10%. The single-threaded build gather and dictionary allocation over a 2M range cost a few ms of serial time.
generality: Inner joins on unique surrogate integer keys where the filtered build side covers 1/16 to 1/2 of its key range. This is common for dimension tables filtered by predicates in star and snowflake queries. Joins with a range up to 1M are unchanged. Joins with very small builds over a wide range can get slower because of the dictionary allocation. The density gate of at most 16x and the memory cap bound that.
risk: Medium. The new code fills the BF outside the normal finalize path. A missed push only costs speed, but a wrong BF hash would give wrong results, so the BF must use exactly the HT's key hash. Memory per HJ grows to range × payload width, which the cap bounds. The off-by-one fix has to be tested with a fully dense build.
